observations.text: SP, due to a departure technique that did not include the briefed climb schedule, did not lead the formation along the published departure track after the air traffic pattern exit, with the result of a 420 feet deviation from the departure altitude and an exit heading error of 16 degrees. The IP directed the correcting turn and flew part of the climb to re-establish the local departure procedure.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not direct the formation safely toward the assigned flight area during the transit. Airspeed diverged by 28 knots from the briefed departure speed and the assigned departure altitude was exceeded by 380 feet. The IP took control of the climb and passed the departure instructions to the wingman.

SP led the climb and departure from the air traffic pattern and the transit to the assigned flight area within the desired standards for the Training Section. Deviations reached the limit values of 300 feet in altitude and 10 degrees on the exit heading, and were recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Marginal performance - earlier recognition of the departure parameters without prompting is expected to improve.

SP led the formation out of the air traffic pattern along the local departure procedure without the IP's verbal prompts. Minor deviations of up to 210 feet in altitude and 14 knots in airspeed were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP directed the formation safely to the assigned flight area, applying the local departure procedures according to LAPs and SOPs. Altitude was held within 110 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and the exit heading within 4 degrees, with accurate and prompt corrections. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned and led the climb, departure and transit to the assigned flight area with exceptional precision, directing the wingman at every briefed point without a single prompt. Deviations were negligible, with altitude held within 40 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and the exit heading within 1 degree. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a power setting at the pattern exit that was not adjusted for the formation climb, did not follow the local departure procedures regarding the air traffic pattern. Airspeed diverged by 26 knots from the briefed departure speed and the formation was displaced 25 degrees off the assigned exit heading. The IP directed the power and heading corrections and flew part of the transit to the assigned flight area.

SP, due to failure to pass a required call at the briefed point, did not direct the formation safely out of the air traffic pattern, leaving the wingman without the briefed climb and departure instructions. The formation exceeded the departure altitude by 450 feet before the deviation was addressed. The IP issued the departure calls and took control of the climb to the assigned flight area.

SP, due to a scan concentrated on the wingman's position instead of the departure parameters, did not maintain the assigned departure altitude and heading during the transit to the flight area. Altitude reached a 300 feet deviation and the exit heading a 10 degree error. Both were recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during the climb out of the air traffic pattern, did not follow the local departure procedure at the prescribed point. Airspeed deviated by 20 knots from the briefed departure speed, at the limit of the allowed value. The correction was applied with delay and only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP led the departure from the air traffic pattern and the transit to the assigned flight area within the desired standards for the Training Section. Minor deviations of up to 240 feet in altitude and 16 knots in airspeed were recognized and corrected without the IP's intervention, but the same altitude excursion appeared twice during the climb. Marginal performance - tighter altitude control during the formation climb is expected to improve.

SP directed the formation safely to the assigned flight area, following the local departure procedures according to LAPs and SOPs. Altitude was maintained within 120 feet, airspeed within 7 knots and the exit heading within 4 degrees, with accurate and timely corrections and standardized direction to the wingman. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP led the climb, departure and transit to the assigned flight area with exceptional precision, keeping the wingman informed at every briefed point. Deviations were negligible, with altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and the exit heading within 2 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a rushed departure sequence in which the climb schedule was applied without reference to the published track, did not follow the local departure procedures regarding the air traffic pattern. The formation was flown 480 feet above the departure altitude and 18 degrees off the assigned exit heading. The IP directed the recovery to the departure track and flew part of the transit to the assigned flight area.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the formation's position relative to the departure track, did not direct the formation safely toward the assigned flight area. The exit heading error grew to 20 degrees and airspeed diverged by 30 knots from the briefed departure speed before any correction was attempted. The IP took control and re-established the departure profile.

SP, due to a trim technique that was not reset after climb power was set, did not hold the assigned departure altitude while leading the formation to the flight area. The deviation reached the 300 feet limit and the exit heading the 10 degree limit. Both were recognized and corrected with delay, following the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to failure to monitor the aircraft state after the configuration change at the pattern exit, did not maintain the briefed departure airspeed during the formation climb. Airspeed reached the 20 knots limit of deviation and the formation drifted to the 10 degree limit on the exit heading. Correction followed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delayed recognition of both deviations.

SP, due to a late power reduction at the level-off, did not capture the departure altitude on the first attempt while leading the formation to the assigned flight area. The deviation reached 230 feet and airspeed 15 knots above the briefed departure speed. Both errors were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to failure to shed a secondary task when workload increased on the departure, did not track the assigned exit heading while coordinating the wingman's position. The heading error reached 8 degrees and altitude deviated by 200 feet from the departure altitude. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention.

SP directed the formation safely to the assigned flight area and followed the local departure procedures with accuracy and speed, holding altitude within 130 feet, airspeed within 9 knots and the exit heading within 5 degrees. The values remained inside the desired standards but close to their limits during the level-off and the turn to the exit heading. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a tighter margin on the departure parameters is expected to improve.

SP led the climb, departure and transit to the assigned flight area with exceptional precision and standardized direction to the wingman throughout. Deviations were negligible, with altitude held within 40 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and the exit heading within 1 degree, and no correction was prompted. Above end of block MIF achieved.
